testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do with a cracked rim?

options.text: Repair it by welding.
Move it to the other dual tire position.
Replace it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Replace it.
questions.explanation: Check your wheels before driving for damage. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe to use.

questions.question: When should you NOT use the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot.
When the brakes are very cold.
When there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: After coming down a steep hill, your brakes may be hot. Do not use the parking brake until they cool down. Using it on hot brakes can damage them.

questions.question: Why should you back a trailer toward the driver's side?

options.text: It gives you a better view.
Backing toward the passenger side is illegal.
Other drivers can help you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when you must back up. This gives you the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through flowing water or a large puddle?

options.text: Speed up.
Gently apply the brakes.
Try to stop in the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Avoid driving through water or large puddles if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and dirt out of your brake system.

questions.question: What vehicle must you use for a driving test for a CDL?

options.text: The same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
Any vehicle, even if it is different from what you will drive.
The testing station will provide the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
questions.explanation: You must use the same type of vehicle for the skills test that you plan to drive. You are responsible for providing the test vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It is not a concern.
It only happens when doing something physical while driving.
It can happen from mental activities like daydreaming.
It is okay on uncrowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen from mental activities like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking to a passenger), or both (like texting). To avoid distracted driving, pre-program your radio, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: What should you do after starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Listen for unusual noises.
Rev the engine.
Release the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: As part of your pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for unusual noises.

questions.question: What should a driver ensure about the truck?

options.text: The truck is overloaded.
The truck is properly loaded.
The cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck is properly loaded.
questions.explanation: Proper loading is essential for safe vehicle operation. Improper loading can affect how the truck handles and can damage it. Improperly loaded cargo can also fall off and hurt or kill people.

questions.question: What could a cardboard box on the roadway contain?

options.text: It is expected to be on the roadway.
It is usually empty and harmless.
A heavy object that could damage vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A heavy object that could damage vehicles.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. Even a cardboard box that looks harmless could contain a heavy object that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air has water in it that collects in the tanks.
To change the pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air has water in it that collects in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the air tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these buildup. Tanks with manual drain valves should be drained at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is a look?

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the instrument panel.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when you open your door, leave your seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During straight line backing, you can only use one look. During other exercises, you can use up to two looks.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right after it starts to rain?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that hasn't washed away yet.
Roads are naturally slippery.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that hasn't washed away yet.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil on the road to create a dangerous, slippery surface.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, what about seat belts?

options.text: You never have to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you are driving a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a seat belt at all times when operating a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Why should you check tires regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
The tread wears down faster in hot weather than in cool weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases when temperature rises. Pay close attention to tire mounting and pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: If a load is 10 feet long, what is the minimum number of tie-downs needed?

options.text: One tie-down.
Two tie-downs.
Three tie-downs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of cargo size.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down quickly with both feet.
Press it down gradually.
Lift it up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually to ensure a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with belts?

options.text: Loosen them.
Check them for tightness.
Scrub them clean.
Leave them alone and don't inspect them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them for tightness.
questions.explanation: Check all belts for tightness and wear. Learn how much looseness is normal for each belt.

questions.question: When traveling downhill, what will your vehicle do?

options.text: Slow down.
Travel at the same speed as on level ground.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to speed up when going downhill. Slow down before you reach a downgrade.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
45 feet
20 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: The right lane.
It doesn't matter which lane you use.
The left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane.
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. When two left turn lanes are available, start your turn in the rightmost lane.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.

options.text: Will always affect
May not affect
Is caused by

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Only required for interstate travel.
Required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Check for emergency equipment during a pre-trip inspection. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Overloading a vehicle with cargo:

options.text: Usually has no effect on the vehicle.
Can affect steering and brake control.
Can affect the electrical system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect steering and brake control.
questions.explanation: Overloading a vehicle can harm steering, braking, and speed control. Learn to recognize when cargo is too heavy or poorly balanced.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible.
Placed as low as possible.
Placed as far to the left as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Cargo placed high makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Place weight as low as possible to keep the vehicle stable.

questions.question: Perform pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time because:

options.text: You will be less likely to forget something.
You will have more time to complete the inspection.
It is required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Using the same order each time helps you learn the steps and remember to check everything. You are less likely to skip a step when you follow a set order.

questions.question: To avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck, you should:

options.text: Switch gears while driving uphill.
Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: You must have an air brake endorsement:

options.text: To use a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.
To transport hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: To use a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brake test to get a license to operate a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: The heavier the vehicle:

options.text: The less important the brakes become.
The harder the brakes need to work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes need to work.
questions.explanation: Heavier vehicles require brakes to work harder to stop.

questions.question: When should mirror adjustments be made?

options.text: Before starting a trip
While driving
When a vehicle is stopped at a traffic signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting a trip
questions.explanation: Check mirrors before each trip. Any trailer should be straight when adjusting mirrors.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule when using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early. Signal well before a turn or lane change.
Signal continuously. Do not cancel a signal until the turn is completed.
Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal.
questions.explanation: Always signal well before turning or changing lanes. Keep the signal on through the entire turn or lane change. Then cancel it. Always signal, even if no one appears to be near you.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the left lane.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Wave your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers. This warns drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your mirrors.
Use your mirrors.
Do not use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors before changing lanes.

questions.question: What can a trailer brake hand valve do on a truck?

options.text: Add fuel to the truck.
Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
Check the engine oil level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops a truck from rolling backward when it is being started from a stop.

questions.question: In hot weather, tar bleeding through pavement is:

options.text: Very slippery.
Just as slippery as the rest of the road.
More slippery than the rest of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very slippery.
questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. These spots are very slippery, so be careful.

questions.question: What emergency equipment must a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if carrying hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When is it okay to text while driving?

options.text: Only on straightaways.
Only in curves.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and not allowed when operating a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: When an engine starts, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Go down.
Go up slowly.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go up slowly.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, the coolant temperature should gradually rise to normal operating level.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air is pumped into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the air storage tanks in an air brake system.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should you NOT do when checking the windshield?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check for windshield cracks and problems. Check wiper arms for proper spring tension and wiper blades for damage or stiff rubber. Do not remove and sharpen the blades.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to keep space between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: No, because it slows traffic flow.
Yes, because it gives you time to react to problems.
Yes, only if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, because it gives you time to react to problems.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides. This gives you time to respond safely if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no higher than three feet.
Should be secured so it does not move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured so it does not move.
questions.explanation: All cargo in a trailer must be secured to prevent it from shifting while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: In a work zone, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Steer with one hand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Always follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if road or weather conditions are bad. Slow down even more if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver crash ahead, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: Stop a safe distance from the crash scene. Wait for police to arrive and report the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: Drivers behind a truck:

options.text: May have trouble seeing objects in front of the truck.
Often have a clear view of the road ahead.
Do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have trouble seeing objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your truck can block the view of drivers behind you. They may not see hazards ahead that make you stop. Flash your brakes and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes.
Stay off the brakes.
Swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Using brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Avoid braking if possible until your vehicle has slowed down significantly.

questions.question: To stay alert while driving, you should:

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Keep the cab warm.
Ride with another driver who can share driving duties.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with another driver who can share driving duties.
questions.explanation: Sharing driving with another driver reduces the risk that either of you will drive while tired. You can also reduce fatigue by avoiding heavy foods and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before you start driving:

options.text: They will likely get clean after you drive a short distance.
It is not a concern.
Clean them before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean them before you drive.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check mirrors and windshields for dirt or anything that blocks your view. Clean them as needed.

questions.question: Strong winds are most likely when:

options.text: Coming out of tunnels.
Going into tunnels.
Driving on shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Coming out of tunnels.
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to keep your vehicle in the correct lane. Wind is especially a problem when driving out of a tunnel.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, they should be:

options.text: Held between you and oncoming traffic.
Carried behind your back so other drivers do not see them until they are placed.
Held as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Held between you and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A driver may have:

options.text: A car license from one state and a CDL from another.
Only one license.
Two licenses: one for cars and one for trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only one license.
questions.explanation: A person cannot have more than one license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.
